decision_maker: Executive Director of Place
purpose:
Over time Wormholt residents have raised
concerns with the Council regarding a significant increase in
traffic volumes, congestion and vehicle speeds on a number of
streets in the ward.

The proposed trial scheme has been developed with significant
input, engagement and coproduction with residents that responds
directly to their issues. A Wormholt resident working group was
established, and a series of workshops held between May 2024 and
June 2025 to identify local issues. A Neighbourhood Have Your Say
Survey was carried out in July 2025 to gain feedback from all
residents on the issues raised, and measures that could be
considered.

Two options have been developed for a trial scheme that introduces
traffic access restrictions in the Wormholt ward. This report
recommends introducing Option 2, a phased trial scheme approach. As
a part of the proposed trial the Council will continue to work
closely with residents and stakeholders to coproduce
solutions.
content:
To launch
a trial Wormholt Neighbourhood traffic safety improvement scheme
that introduces traffic access restrictions for non-borough
residents via an Experimental Traffic Order (ETO).

 

To
implement Option 2 as the preferred approach to introduce traffic
access restrictions, enforced by Automatic Number Plate Recognition
(ANPR) cameras (see Proposal and Analysis of Options section below
for details). Option 2 is the implementation of a phased trial
scheme with traffic restrictions on the following
streets:


Phase 1
                            
i.    
Steventon Road at the junction with Old Oak
Road
                           
ii.    
Bryony Road at the junction with Bloemfontein
Road
                         
iii.    
Sawley
Road at the junction with Bloemfontein
Road
 

Phase 2
                         
iv.    
Bloemfontein Road south of the junction with South
Africa Road- initially to be kept in data monitoring to help
understand traffic patterns during the trial; enforcement may be activated
if any potential traffic displacement becomes a longer-term
issue.
 

To delegate authority to the Director of Climate Change and Transport
to monitor traffic, consider consultation feedback
provided during the experiment and make any amendments or
adjustments to the scheme during the experimental period and in
line with the statutory process.

 

To delegate authority
to Director of Climate Change and
Transport to work with residents, businesses, and other
stakeholders to develop a long-term vision for the Wormholt ward
and the wider area.


This trial aims to improve road
safety and air quality by achieving a significant reduction in
total traffic volumes and through traffic on residential streets.
It seeks to achieve this by discouraging out-of-borough traffic
from using residential streets accessed via the A40 Westway and Old
Oak Road, as cut through routes.
 
The trial makes progress
towards achieving the Council’s policy agenda for Public
Health and the Climate Emergency, and the Council’s
priorities, with twenty-six direct links and fifteen non-direct
links.
 
Working with resident groups
and engaging the wider community on the proposals has helped the
Council build a better understanding of the local situation and
design a tailored and area specific trial.
 
The trial can be amended,
altered, or abandoned without significant capital investment on
infrastructure or making permanent changes to the road
network.
 
The collection of real-time and
automatic traffic count data during the trial scheme will inform
decision-making. Any future recommendation to make the trial
permanent or to abandon it will be based on data and feedback
collected during the trial.
 
The experimental trial is
estimated to cost £36,000, and the period will be between six
and eighteen months, as required. Should there be a future
recommendation that the trial becomes permanent, any additional one
off and/or ongoing costs will be considered as part of that future
decision report.

Option 1 proposes the
introduction of trial measures at all identified cut-through routes
at the same time. This includes traffic access restrictions on the
following streets:

·      
Steventon Road at the junction with Old Oak
Road

·      
Bryony Road at the junction with Bloemfontein
Road

·      
Sawley
Road at the junction with Bloemfontein
Road

·      
Bloemfontein Road south of the junction with South
Africa Road
 
Option 2 introduces measures at
identified cut-through routes in a two phased approach.
 
The
full options analysis can be found in the report

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Housing and Homelessness
purpose:
In relation to our term-service contract for
asbestos which is due to expire on the 27th of September 2025 we
are seeking approval to:
1) Extend the contract by 24 months. This extension is allowed in
line with the contract provisions.
2) Modify the overall contract sum for the entire 7 year term from
£2,250,000 to £2,470,173.84.
content:
1.    
Approve the extension of the existing Asbestos removal and
remediation contract for 24 months from Friday, 1 August 2025 to
Saturday, 31 July 2027 with Cablesheer
Limited.
 
2.    
Approve an increase in the contract value (for both initial
contract period and extension period) from £1,382,341.33 to
£1,820,963.33.
 

1.    
The Council has a legal obligation to ensure its
properties are maintained and that any risks to health are being
appropriately managed and actioned.
 
2.    
Consistent with other social landlords, the
Council’s assets still contain substantial asbestos
containing materials. Survey records show that 87% of blocks
(communal areas) and a considerable proportion of dwellings contain
asbestos and all school buildings constructed prior to 2000 contain
asbestos materials.
 
3.    
Whilst asbestos in good condition can remain in
situ, the Council’s active programme of upgrade and
improvement works together with routine reactive repairs mean that
there is an ongoing requirement for the removal of asbestos. Annual
asbestos re-inspections to blocks and schools in line with the
requirements of Regulation 4 of the Control of Asbestos Regulations
2012 also identify asbestos that requires removal or
remediation.
 
4.    
The Council’s Asbestos Management Plan details
processes to be followed in the event of an emergency involving
asbestos and these are incumbent on the response of the Licensed
Asbestos Removal Contractor attending and making safe.
 
5.    
As asbestos removal and remediation is key to the operational
processes of all workstreams it is important that this work is
completed on time and to the required standards. Cablesheer Ltd.
have provided a consistent and reliable service for both routine
work and emergencies over the initial term of the contract.
 
6.    
The existing contract award was based on a competitive procurement
process in line with the Public Contracts Regulations 2015. The
Final Tenders received were evaluated by the Council’s
evaluation team against published evaluation criteria. As the
Contractor recommended for appointment, Cablesheer Ltd. were
identified as the most economically advantageous tenderer, having
applied the evaluation criteria.
 
7.    
Reprocuring the asbestos removal and remediation
contract with an alternative supplier is unlikely to result in cost
savings or improvements in performance so the extension to the
existing contract is recommended.
 

Please refer to the report.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Housing and Homelessness has decided to approve the extension of the Asbestos removal and remediation contract with Cablesheer Limited.

content:
Recommendation to establish
time banded collections for businesses that are based in two major
high streets in the borough. Time banding regulations will create
specific time slots throughout any given 24-hour period, when
businesses can present their waste and recycling bags out on the
public highway for collection.

1.    
To agree to undertake a consultation including the businesses and
waste collectors operating in King Street and Uxbridge Road about
the introduction of specific time bands for waste collections in
these streets
 
2.    
To delegate authority to the Executive Director of Place, in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for Public Realm, to consider
the outcome of the consultation, to decide whether to proceed to
implement time band arrangements and if it is decided to do so to
finalise the time band arrangements adopt the necessary regulations
and proceed to implementation of the scheme.
 
3.    
To award a contract to the preferred supplier detailed in Exempt
Appendix 1 to undertake the proposed consultation, for the cost
also detailed in Exempt Appendix 1.
 

1.    
The decision to implement commercial waste time
banding is to reduce the amount of visible waste on the streets in
our town centres. This will benefit everyone, including the
businesses, as it makes these streets a more pleasant and
accessible place to be.
 
2.    
Whilst it is accepted that the placing of bags of
waste out for collection is a necessity, an unregulated situation
whereby bags can be present at any point during a 24 hour period,
is not conducive to having the cleanest, best maintained streets in
London nor to providing pleasant and accessible spaces for local
residents, customers of local businesses and other visitors to our
high streets.
 
3.    
The Council is able to use powers available to it to introduce time
banded collections of waste and recycling from designated business
premises in the borough.
 

Please refer to the report.

That Cabinet approved
the draft Local Plan Regulation 18 for public consultation
(Appendix 1).

 

That Cabinet gave
delegated authority to the Director of Planning and Property, in
consultation with the Cabinet Member for the Economy, to make any
necessary editorial amendments and minor changes to the appendices
prior to consultation.

 

That Cabinet approved
the adoption and publication of the attached revised Local
Development Scheme (Appendix 2) to reflect the adjusted Local Plan
timetable.

 

That Cabinet approved
the updated Statement of Community Involvement (SCI) for adoption
(Appendix 3).

 

That Cabinet noted
that the evidence base documents (listed in this report) will be
published alongside the regulation 18 Local Plan.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the draft Local Plan Regulation 18 for public consultation and adopt the revised Local Development Scheme and Statement of Community Involvement.

purpose:
The Council is required to use funds received
from planning obligations to address the impact of developments
carried out . This report sets out the use of funds received
through Section 106 agreements and received as a result of the
Community Infrastructure Levy (CIL) schedules in force in the
Borough. It seeks approval to the drawdown of these funds for
projects which have been delivered in 2024/25.
content:
1.   
That Cabinet approved the 2024/25 drawdown of
Section 106 and Community Infrastructure Levy monies as set out in
this report, to fund expenditure of £22,413,499 for a wide
range of community benefits across the borough.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve the drawdown of funds to fund community benefits in the borough.
